summary: This short program stores a person's name in a variable and joins it onto a greeting so the message prints as one line of text. It is the starting point for a welcome application, before any user input is involved.

lines.text: The name lives in a regular local variable, not a final constant, so the host can swap in whichever guest is arriving and run the program again.
The + here is string concatenation: the literal text and the variable's value are assembled into a single string before printing, the way you would paste cut-out words together to form a note.
Notice the space inside the quotes after "Welcome". Concatenation adds nothing of its own, so leaving that space out would print "WelcomeAda".
